# A ball from a one-limb center and a radius

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/*/brute/, results/brute-code.json and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `ball_make_1` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

The ball of center $c$ and radius $r$, or the empty set or the whole line when they do not make a finite ball:

$$Z = \{\, t : \lvert t - c\rvert \le r \,\}.$$

## C++

| Form | Operands | Result | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Ball<T, 1>(c, r)` | `Expansion<T, 1>`, `T` | `Ball<T, 1>` |  |
| `Ball<T, 1>(c)` | `Expansion<T, 1>` | `Ball<T, 1>` | implicit: the point $c$, radius 0 |
| `Ball<T, 1>(a)` | `T` | `Ball<T, 1>` | implicit: the point $a$, radius 0 |
| `Ball<T, 1>(q)` | `Constant<Expansion<T, 1>>` | `Ball<T, 1>` | explicit: center `q.value`, radius `q.error`, for `q` a result of `rational` or `integer`; `constexpr`; does not round |

`T` is `float` or `double`; the operations are in namespace `kairn`, header `kairn/kairn.hpp`. The operators and functions also accept the marker `kairn::unverified` on an operand, which they need while the kernel is UNVERIFIED (a constructor does not take it).

## Requires

- $c$ is any value of `T`: a number, $\pm\infty$ or a NaN.
- $r$ is any value of `T`: a number, $\pm\infty$ or a NaN.

## Guarantees

For operands that satisfy the requirements, finite, infinite or NaN:

- The result $Z$, of center $c_w$ and radius $r_w$, is a canonical ball.
- $Z$ is the empty set (every limb a NaN) when $r$ is negative, $-\infty$ included.
- Otherwise $Z$ is the whole line (center 0, radius $+\infty$) when $r$ is a NaN or $+\infty$, or $c$ is not finite.
- Otherwise $Z$ is the ball of center $c$ and radius $r$, exactly.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 1 bit, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the IEEE model, with signed zeros, infinities, NaN and overflow. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `ball_make_1_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/IeeeMake.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/IeeeMake.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions ball_make_1_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proof of `ball_make_1_correct` depends on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** constructors (Milestone 1 listing; a NaN radius the whole line, 2026-11-20). **License:** algorithm: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/ball_make_1.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/ball_make_1.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal model (`proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).

```
# A ball from a one-limb center and a radius, both from the program and both guarded (rule R3):
# ball_make_2 with the center guarded as well, here c0 = guard(c), and no k1 (milestone1.md,
# "Values that enter from the program"). The empty set when the radius is negative, -infinity
# included (n true); otherwise the whole line when the center is not finite or the radius is
# +infinity or a NaN (f false: lt(g, const inf) is false for a NaN), as a NaN bound given to an
# interval is (the owner's decision of 2026-11-20); otherwise the ball itself. The ordinary case is
# the first arm of each select (ok = not(n)), as the scalar printer's branch over a fix-up wants.

g   = guard(r)
c0  = guard(c)
n   = lt(g, 0)
ok  = not(n)
a   = abs(c0)
f1  = lt(a, const inf)
f2  = lt(g, const inf)
f   = and(f1, f2)
k0  = select(f, c0, 0)
s   = select(f, g, const inf)
cw  = select(ok, k0, const nan)
rw  = select(ok, s, const nan)
```

## Measured

The stored brute-force runs of this kernel's code: the oracle judged, in exact arithmetic, the results of the compiled kernel (every compiler, scalar and packed code, every contraction setting) on random operands of `binary64` and `binary32`, and those of the generator's interpreter on every operand of small formats. A measurement, not a bound. A run is shown only if it ran the code the kernel has now: its generated C++ (scalar and packed, every kernel it calls inlined, with the functions it calls; comments left out) must be the same at the commit of the run, as the fingerprints in [`results/brute-code.json`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/results/brute-code.json) show ([How to read a page](reading.md#what-the-measured-numbers-are)).

**Milestone 2**: the runs of commit `5f597fb`, from the stored summaries in [`results/milestone2/brute/`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/tree/main/results/milestone2/brute) ([the report](../developer/results/brute-milestone2.md#ball_make_1)).
They judged the kernel in the extended domain, infinite and NaN operands included, as the oracle reads its statement in the IEEE model ([Claims of the non-finite layer](../developer/architecture.md#claims-of-the-non-finite-layer)).

| Run | Cases judged | Failed |
|---|---|---|
| `binary64` (`double`), compiled: 90 runners on 3 machines | 103 500 000 | 0 |
| `binary32` (`float`), compiled: 90 runners on 3 machines | 103 500 000 | 0 |
| toy formats, every operand: 6 domains of 6 formats | 6 416 804 | 0 |

The runs of Milestone 1, at commits `6f89054` and `f7e0b6d`, were of other code, and are not counted.

## Not claimed

- Anything for operands that do not satisfy the requirements.
- The sign of a zero limb, and which NaN a NaN result is: the claims compare neither.
